cohort: The study included 8,572 deliveries conducted in 2019 at a private hospital in Athens, involving women classified in Robson 1 and 2a categories.
finding: The study identified several clinical and demographic predictors for cesarean section rates in women classified in Robson 1 and 2a categories, including smoking, IVF, pre-existing maternal conditions, fetal pathology, maternal age, gestational age, Greek nationality, gestational diabetes, and neonatal birth weight.
mod_finding: Smoking, IVF, pre-existing maternal conditions, fetal pathology, specific maternal age and gestational age ranges, Greek nationality, gestational diabetes, and neonatal birth weight were identified as significant predictors for the mode of birth (cesarean section) in Robson 1 and 2a categories.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weights ranging from below 3,000 g to 4,000 g or more were included and analyzed as predictors for CS.
gest_age: Gestational ages from 37+0 to 41+6 weeks were included and analyzed as predictors for CS.
